newsitem.title: CHINA: China convertible bonds could succeed- specialists.
newsitem.headline: China convertible bonds could succeed- specialists.

text.p: China's plans to develop a convertible bond market could be successful despite rules limiting issuers to unlisted companies, officials and financial specialists said on Saturday.

They said China's plans to allow up to four billion yuan ($481.9 million) worth of convertible corporate bonds needed institutional support and a legal framework, but the scheme could provide funds for many cash-short state enterprises.
"I see prospects for this market," said C.Y. Huang, director of investment banking at Credit Lyonnais Securities (Asia) Ltd.
"These are a complex financial product..," he said after a seminar on convertible bonds. "You need institutional investors. That is the first step."
China has said it would allow some of its 500 biggest firms to offer bonds that would be convertible into stock. The offers would have to be worth at least 100 million yuan.
Initially, Beijing would limit issuers to unlisted companies, though it intended to push these firms toward public stock offers eventually.

Investors would bear additional risk over the timing and pricing of conversion as the bonds would be offered before the issuing company had shares traded on either of the nation's domestic stock markets.
A securities regulator who asked not to be identified said China needed to have a framework so that issuing companies would know when they would get a quota to list their shares.
China sets an annual quota of share listings, and companies must obtain a portion of the quota in order to offer their stock to the public.
The official also said many of the state-run companies that Beijing wanted to help raise funds were already heavily in debt and might have difficulty issuing bonds.
But the official believed convertible bonds could be a way to raise funds for state companies.
"This could be one avenue for state companies to raise cash," said the securities regulator.
